body.page: 原书 PDF 第 428 页
zh: 本书分析的大部分日记是随着“重建”（perestroika）期间苏联档案馆开放以及1991年苏联解体，才得以供学者查阅的。其中一些来自前苏联国家和党政档案馆。尽管这些日记是由忠于苏联政权的政治活动家、作家和艺术家创作的，但由于担心其具有煽动性的内容，它们一直被列为机密，直到该政权结束。另一些日记长期以来就可以在国家档案馆查阅。还有一些来自“社会档案馆”，这些档案馆是在政权崩溃期间成立的，用于存放受迫害个人和政治团体的文献收藏，或收集普通苏联公民的个人文件。这些非官方机构迅速建立起规模可观的自传记录库，与国家馆藏中往往占主导地位的行政和机构视角形成对照。还有一些个人记录是由幸存的日记作者本人或其家属提供的。本书详述的几本日记来自私人档案，在一些情况下，我有幸见到了日记作者。我们的谈话总是内容丰富、引人入胜，尽管有时在观点和解释上也存在分歧。这些日记作者的积极参与鲜明地提醒我们：将与作者生活息息相关的文献当作历史资料，会带来伦理上的挑战。
en: Most of the diaries analyzed in this book became available to scholars with the opening of the Soviet archives during perestroika and after the implosion of the Soviet Union in 1991. Some of them are from former Soviet state and party archives. Though composed by political activists, writers, and artists loyal to the Soviet regime, they remained classified until the end of that regime for fear of their incendiary content. Others had been accessible in state archives for a long time. Still others come from “social archives,” which were founded during the collapse of the regime to house documentary collections of persecuted individuals and political groups, or to collect personal documents from ordinary Soviet citizens. These unofficial institutions quickly built a sizeable inventory of autobiographical records that provide a counterpoint to the administrative and institutional perspectives that tend to predominate in state repositories. Yet other personal records have been made available by surviving diarists themselves or their families. Several of the diaries discussed at length in this book are from private archives, and in a number of cases I was also fortunate enough to meet the diarists. Our conversations were invariably rich and fascinating, though not always free of clashes in opinion and interpretation. The active involvement of these diarists served as a vocal reminder of the ethical challenges involved in treating as historical sources documents which form an intimate part of their authors’ lives.

body.page: 原书 PDF 第 429 页
zh: 已知的斯大林时代的个人记录数量惊人，但这似乎只是冰山一角。最大的未开发宝库是前内务人民委员部（斯大林时期的秘密警察）的中央和地方档案馆，外国研究人员目前几乎仍无法进入。从这些档案馆中发掘出的少数几本日记带有国家检察人员画下的线和批注，从中可以洞察日记作者的记录是如何被接收和解读的。无数其他日记散布在后苏联地区的私人家庭中。有理由担心，其中许多记录可能永远无法被学者利用，因为它们现在的拥有者没有意识到其历史意义，认为它们是极其隐私的记录、笨拙的散文练习或转瞬即逝的文字，不宜让历史学家看到。
en: Impressive in number, the known personal records from the Stalin era appear to form only the tip of an iceberg. The greatest untapped repositories are the central and regional archives of the former NKVD, the Stalinist secret police, to which foreign researchers still have virtually no access. The few diaries that have been unearthed from these archives bear underlinings and remarks made by state prosecutors that offer insights into how the diarists’ recordings were received and interpreted. Innumerable other diaries are scattered in private households across the post-Soviet realm. There is reason to fear that many of these records may never become available to scholars, because their current owners are unaware of their historical significance and consider them intensely personal records, awkward exercises in prose, or ephemeral texts, unfit for the historian’s eye.

body.page: 原书 PDF 第 429 页
zh: 持续收集并编目反映苏联过去的自传记录，必定会带来丰富的收获——大量的个人文件，不仅来自斯大林早期，也来自战争年代和战后几十年。人们正在努力建立这样的目录，但其成效如何仍有待观察。“纪念”和“人民档案馆”等组织长期经费不足，主要依靠其少数工作人员的热情和顽强坚持而生存。他们必须应对正在痛苦适应市场经济、并已失去对社会和文化认同问题的大部分兴趣的社会环境。使历史意识下降问题更加严重的是，俄罗斯当时的政治领导人不愿正视共产党政权的遗产，也不愿面对政治连续性和道德责任等根本问题。正视这些问题会引发辩论并带来社会分裂的风险，但辩论本身的内容也将培育政治民主蓬勃发展所依赖的那种公民文化。
en: A sustained initiative to collect and inventory the autobiographical record of the Soviet past would surely yield great riches—scores of personal documents, not just from the early Stalin period but from the war years and the postwar decades as well. Some efforts are being made to create such inventories, but what they will achieve remains to be seen. Organizations like “Memorial” and the “People’s Archive” are chronically underfunded and survive largely thanks to the enthusiasm and dogged persistence of their small staffs. They must contend with a social environment that is painfully adapting to the market economy and has lost much of its former interest in questions of social and cultural identity. Compounding this drop in historical awareness is the reluctance of Russia’s current political leaders to come to terms with the legacy of the Communist regime and confront fundamental issues of political continuity and moral responsibility. To confront such issues would stir debate and risk social divisions, but the very terms of the debate would also foster the type of civic culture on which a political democracy can thrive.

body.page: 原书 PDF 第 429、430 页
zh: 接触来自苏联过去的自传性声音的批判性学术研究，无法回避它们在当今的反响。在分析斯大林时代的日记时，至关重要的是要反思不断变化的政治局势，这些局势解释了为什么在特定时间，特定文件被认为具有历史价值，从而被保存在档案馆或以出版形式展示。这种批判性的视角也有助于我们注意到那些不符合当时历史和政治利益，因此没有进入档案馆或出版物的隐形个人资料。虽然在斯大林政权鼎盛时期出版的日记和回忆录无一例外地将作者描绘成热情的苏联公民，但在后斯大林时代的解冻时期，日记中的英雄变得更加复杂。1962年出版的尼娜·科斯特琳娜（Nina Kosterina）的日记就是一例。科斯特琳娜是一名莫斯科女学生和共青团员，在第二次世界大战中作为游击队员牺牲，她在日记中写道，她很难接受父亲在1937年作为“人民公敌”被捕的事实。科斯特琳娜的英雄主义在于，尽管在个人生活中遭受了痛苦和不公，她仍继续忠于共产主义价值。在呼应赫鲁晓夫改革精神的背景下，“重建”初期出版的日记展现了在斯大林主义下受难但仍捍卫党的价值的忠诚共产党员。随着“重建”的失败，更多批评苏联体制的日记得以出版，学者们开始将日记视为反抗斯大林主义的阵地。
en: Critical scholarship engaging autobiographical voices from the Soviet past cannot avoid their present-day reverberations. In analyzing Stalin-era diaries, it is crucial to reflect on the changing political conjunctures that account for why, at a particular time, particular documents are deemed to be of historical value and therefore are preserved in archives or showcased in published form. Such a critical perspective also helps us register the invisible personal sources that do not conform to the historical and political interests of their day and therefore do not make their way into an archive or a publication. Whereas diaries and memoirs published at the height of the Stalinist regime invariably portrayed their authors as enthusiastic Soviet citizens, during the post-Stalin thaw the diaristic hero acquired more complexity. Witness the publication of Nina Kosterina’s diary in 1962. Kosterina, a Moscow schoolgirl and komsomolist who died as a partisan in the Second World War, wrote in her diary of her difficulty in coming to terms with her father’s arrest in 1937 as an “enemy of the people.” Kosterina’s heroism consisted in her continued devotion to Communist values despite the distress and injustice she suffered in her personal life. Invoking the spirit of Khrushchev’s reforms, diaries published in the early perestroika period featured devoted Communist diarists who suffered under Stalinism but nevertheless defended the values of the party. As perestroika failed, diaries more critical of the Soviet order appeared in print, and scholars began to study diaries as sites of resistance to Stalinism.

body.page: 原书 PDF 第 430 页
zh: 日记在书写和改写斯大林时期的经验中一直发挥着并将继续发挥积极作用。当今围绕历史再现的政治，也影响着把个人证词作为历史证据的历史学家的工作。尽管如此，历史学家能够采取批判性的立场，通过反思政治和认识论的转变，来解释为什么某本日记在特定时间被认为具有价值并因此被保留在档案馆或出版。这样的视角有助于我们评价档案或文献出版物，将其视为一个建立起来的记忆构建场域，而非通向过去的透明窗口，它与当下的政治和道德问题密切相关。
en: Diaries have played and continue to play an active role in the writing and rewriting of the experience of the Stalin period. Present-day politics of historical representation also affect the work of historians who consult personal testimonies as historical evidence. Still, historians are able to adopt a critical stance, by reflecting on the political and epistemological shifts that explain why a given diary is deemed to be of interest at a given time and why it is hence retained in an archive or published. Such a perspective helps us appraise an archive or a documentary publication, not as a transparent window into the past, but as an instituted site of memory construction, heavily implicated in the political and moral questions of the present.
